mike_customer: Hey team — started seeing our embeddings index fail after a deploy. Previously embeddings were 1536, now responses are 1024. No schema change on our side. Happened ~2026-02-05 14:12 UTC. Anyone seen this?

sara_support: Hi @mike_customer — sorry about that. Can you paste a sample request id/response or a minimal repro? Also which model string are you calling?

mike_customer: model we call: "redwood-embed-large-legacy:2025-11-01" (we pinned it during onboarding). Sample response (redacted):
```json
{
  "request_id": "r-0b2c3d4e",
  "model": "redwood-embed-large-legacy:2025-11-01",
  "data": { "embedding": { "length": 1024, "values": [0.001, ...] } }
}
```
We index that into our vector DB and it errors because index expects 1536 dims.

devon_eng: thanks @mike_customer. Quick thought: if the pinned variant was substituted server-side to a lower-capacity variant during a capacity fallback, it can change output shape. Can you share the full response headers (particularly any x-redwood-* headers)?

mike_customer: headers from the call: 
```
x-request-id: r-0b2c3d4e
x-redwood-variant: redwood-embed-small:2026-01-15
x-served-region: us-west-2
content-type: application/json
```
So looks like the variant was different than the model param we sent.

sara_support: that header confirms a variant substitution. Sorry — we should have surfaced that to you. I'm escalating to runtime. @devon_eng can you check if a fallback substitution policy recently changed for reserved capacity?

devon_eng: looking now. There's a recent autoswap rule for customers on reserved pools when bursting to best-effort; it prefers lower-cost smaller variants if dedicated capacity is exhausted. That rule shouldn't flip pinned variants, but I see an exception path where pinned references to legacy back-compat names were mapped to a compatible modern variant that has a different embed dim.

mike_customer: ugh — that explains it. Any immediate mitigation? We can't reindex quickly.

julia_oncall: mitigation options: 1) Force the exact variant by calling the fully qualified model id that includes the immutable hash (we can provide it), 2) Temporarily route you to hosted capacity where your pinned version is still available, or 3) we'll open an emergency rollback of the substitution rule for your org. Which do you prefer?

mike_customer: prefer option 1 or 2. Option 2 is fine short-term. How do we switch?

sara_support: to test hosted route quickly, set header `x-redwood-route: hosted` on your requests OR update the SDK call to specify deployment=\"hosted\". Example curl to force hosted: 
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \
  -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY\" \
  -H \"x-redwood-route: hosted\" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-large-legacy:2025-11-01","input":"hello"}'
```
If you get embedding length 1536 in that response, hosted has the expected variant.

mike_customer: running that now...

deploy-bot: deploy event: autoscaling-policy-update applied to reserved-pool-42 at 2026-02-05T14:08:22Z (change-id: ch-99f1)

mike_customer: Hosted forced response returns length 1536. Good.

sara_support: OK — short-term workaround: set `x-redwood-route: hosted` in your production clients until we patch the substitution logic. We'll also push a targeted fix so pinned/immutable names never map to variants with different output shapes.

devon_eng: root cause notes for follow-up: pinned legacy tags were being resolved via an alias table; during alias resolution we matched to the nearest semver-compatible variant which in some cases was a smaller embed model. Plan: add a strict-compatibility check (embedding dim + schema) on alias resolution and emit an event when substitution happens. We'll also add a monitoring alert for any embedding-dim changes per org.

julia_oncall: I've opened INC-2026-013 and assigned to eng-runtime; added customer impact  P1. We'll track with the customer until fixed.

mike_customer: Thanks everyone. Please keep me posted. Our index job has been paused.

sara_support: will do — I'll follow up in this thread with the immutable model id and ETA for the runtime patch. :thumbsup:
